messages.subject: Further input advice
messages.body_plain:
Dear Sir,

Thank you for the most interesting paper and for releasing your code.

I have a couple of questions on which I would really appreciate your response.

In your examples you seem to only list one CNA per chromosome. Please can you give an example of multiple CNA per chromosome? Would you still have multiple row names of Chr1 or would you create unique identifiers?

Secondly in your ‘Y’ dataframe displaying whether SNAa are affected by CNAs there doesn’t seem to be a way of specifying this on a per sample basis. Please can you help me understand this dataframe further.

Many thanks and kind regards,

Simon

Dr Simon Rodney

messages.subject: Re: [canopy_phylogeny] Further input advice
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. For your first question, if the two CNA events don’t overlap in a chromosome, then they should be treated as separate events. If they overlap, you should refer to our GitHub page https://github.com/yuchaojiang/Canopy  in terms of how to generate the input.

For your second question, Y matrix is not per sample based. For all the SNA and CNA input, you know whether SNA lies in the CNA but of course each sample may have different SNA and CNA but the physical locations of SNA won’t change with regard to the CNAs.

Hope that this clarifies and let me know if you have further question.

Yuchao

messages.subject_clean: [yuchaojiang/Canopy] Some questions about major copy number and minor copy number? (#1)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks for your interest in Canopy. Mutect only outputs somatic point mutations. For allele-specific copy number (ASCN) estimates, we recommend Sequenza. After you call ASCN, you can refer to our GitHub page for how to further generate the major and minor copy numbers.

Best,
Yuchao
